stepNotes.1: Reviewed the twenty assigned utility files inside the broader 54-file util unit, covering pure helpers, process-wide limits, filesystem operations, and file-lock state.
stepNotes.2: Child environments, archive arguments, directory headers, and lexical path containment were traced as trust boundaries; sanitization and PowerShell quoting are explicit, while symlink safety remains caller-owned.
stepNotes.3: Atomic write and decode/error fallbacks are sound; tiny-width truncate output can exceed max, and Context.use rejects generic falsy values because it uses a truthiness check.
stepNotes.4: Semaphore handoff and fan-out cleanup are safe, but stale FileLock stealing can unlink a newly acquired owner between body read and deletion because acquisition identity is not revalidated.
stepNotes.5: Concurrency workers, outbound caps, Git retries, and upward traversal all have finite bounds; globUp may scan once per ancestor but terminates at stop or root.
stepNotes.6: Archive, glob, Git, schema-wrapper, and disposal responsibilities stay within narrow helpers; lock-token/revalidation work belongs in filelock and process-lock rather than storage callers.
stepNotes.7: Temporary-file cleanup preserves primary errors, fn contains a redundant catch/rethrow, writeStream currently has tests but no production caller, and broad short-message abort matching can hide genuine failures.
stepNotes.8: No Critical item or finding note exists; recorded non-Critical follow-ups are the stale-lock race, tiny truncation widths, falsy context values, and interrupt false positives, with targeted test gaps identified.
stepNotes.9: Focused verification passed 15 Vitest files and 158 tests with one platform skip; primary reviewer artifacts are complete and no Critical-triggered reverify file is required.
